definition: Folk psychology is the study of the mental life and mental products of races, nations, or similar social groups, especially among so-called primitive peoples. It overlaps with anthropology and folk-lore by focusing on things like myth, legend, religion, and other forms of collective thought, and it was historically contrasted with social psychology.
